answer: Each agent must keep a hash-linked heartbeat: every signed pulse carries a fresh nonce and the digest of the previous pulse, so a botnet cannot backfill months of history in one afternoon. Unpredictable zephyr audits then require the live key to recompute the next link inside a short deadline; a missed reply freezes rewards. If many aliases emit a synchronized ripple of identical intervals, a randomly drawn falcon panel of established agents can slash a joint bond posted at registration. Cheap key generation survives; staffing a distinct always-on responder for each puppet does not.
